title: Proactive Ejection Windows with Soft Capacity Escrow and Latency-Graded Routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a proactive ejection window mechanism combined with a soft capacity escrow and latency-graded routing tiers to reduce cross-region blast radius during transient overloads while preserving tail-latency SLOs. This ticket covers: 1) policy surface and config, 2) runtime admission hooks (soft escrow tokens), 3) eviction heuristics that respect per-tenant geo-pinning, and 4) safe rollout & telemetry for validating SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: Config API exposes ejection_window (seconds), escrow_fraction (0-1), latency_grade thresholds, and geo_pin_enforcement options.
Runtime can reserve soft escrow tokens per-region and per-customer that are consumed during short overload windows and returned when pressure eases.
Latency-graded routing will demote requests progressively to wider-region pools based on quantile breaches (p50/p95/p99) and escrow exhaustion.
No user-visible increase >10% in p99 tail latency for customers with geo_pin_enforcement enabled during a controlled overload test compared to baseline.
Observability: new Dashboards show escrow utilization, ejection window events, per-region admission rejections, and SLO delta charts.
Automated canary run produces a pass signal on region failover simulation and staged rollout policy.
Playbook updated: steps for emergency rollback, manual and automatic drain, and SLA communication templates.
design_decisions: Use soft escrow (fractional token) instead of hard admission to allow small bursts to proceed without immediate shed when capacity fluctuates.
Ejection window is time-bound (configurable 5-30s) so transient noise does not cause long-lived evictions.
Routing will prefer local pools while honoring geo_pin tags; when escrow exhausted, expand fanout to adjacent regions based on latency_grade tiers rather than immediate global failover.
Prefer probabilistic early-drop for low-priority requests during sustained overloads; preserve deterministic behavior for P0 customers via bypass flags.
Telemetry-first approach: coarse rollout with 0.1% of cross-region traffic for initial validation, then gradual to 10% before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Admission hook to be implemented in steering service (steerbox) - lightweight state kept in local egress metadata cache.
Escrow token bookkeeping persists to regional Redis with 200ms TTL refresh; design to tolerate Redis miss by reverting to conservative shedding.
Introduce new routing decision state 'ejection_window_active' propagated via request headers for downstream tracing.
Backwards compatibility: default escrow_fraction=0 (no change) so rollout is opt-in per-customer/route.
Edge-case: cross-tenant noisy-neighbor scenarios require per-tenant hard caps; add later as follow-up if telemetry shows frequent eviction by few tenants.
tradeoffs: Soft escrow reduces false-positive shedding but increases complexity in bookkeeping and potential state divergence across regions.
Time-bounded ejection windows avoid long-term churn but may permit short bursts that briefly oversubscribe capacity if windows align poorly.
Latency-graded routing reduces global fanout but can increase cross-region latency for demoted requests; acceptable for low-priority routes but not for strict SLO routes.
test_plan: Unit tests for escrow token allocation/deallocation and TTL refresh logic.
Integration test simulating region spike where local capacity drops to 60% and verifying escrow consumption semantics and subsequent refill behavior.
Chaos test: kill regional allocator to ensure routing gracefully demotes requests per latency_grade tiers and SLO deltas recorded.
Performance test measuring decision latency overhead (<1ms 95th) for steering decision path.
Regression test against geo_pin enforcement to ensure pinned customers are not evicted unexpectedly.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature gated off in prod, deploy components to all regions (no config enabled).
Phase 1: Enable for internal/test orgs with escrow_fraction=0.2, ejection_window=10s, observe 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Canary 0.1% of external traffic, add telemetry dashboards and alerting thresholds for escrow>70% and ejection_rate spikes.
Phase 3: Incremental ramp to 10% then 50% with weekly SLO reviews; hold if p99 regresses by >5% for geo-pinned customers.
Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecation of older emergency-shed paths after 30 days of stable metrics.
telemetry_requirements: Per-region escrow utilization gauge (per-tenant and aggregate).
Ejection event counter with labels: region, customer_id (hashed), route, reason (latency|capacity|manual).
Routing decision log sample (1/1000) with decision path, candidate pools, telemetry at decision time.
SLO delta dashboard: baseline vs current p50/p95/p99 by customer cohort and by route.
Alerts: escrow_utilization > 80% for 3 consecutive minutes in multiple regions, ejection_rate > threshold.
operational_playbook: If ejection_rate spikes: 1) check regional autoscaler and queue backpressure metrics 2) temporarily reduce escrow_fraction for affected customers 3) open incident and communicate to ops.
Manual rollback: flip feature flag off, which causes immediate stop of new ejection windows and drains escrow tokens naturally; follow with emergency scaling if needed.
Post-incident: collect top offending routes and tenants, consider per-tenant hard caps and conservative geo_pin overrides.
